text:
maya: Heads-up — after last week's driver+fw push in us-west we started seeing intermittent card flicker on a subset of A100s. Not constant XID storms, more like short ECC-correctable bursts followed by kernel oops on one process. Repro rate ~3% of pods on affected hosts.

sanjay: Can you paste the smallest repro log and the node IDs?

maya: Node IDs: compute-usw-107, compute-usw-112, compute-usw-129. Small log snippet below (from kernel ring buffer on compute-usw-112):

```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: GPU panic: Serializing GPU reset
[ 1234.567893] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid=21872, name=gpt-worker
[ 1234.567899] NVRM: Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1235.000011] kernel: NVRM: ECC correctable error count increase on GPU 0
```

maya: Driver version rolled: `525.85.12` + fw `v1.2.4` (canaryed clusterwide on Tue night).

liam: Thanks. Quick telemetry query I ran (prometheus):

```
sum by (node) (increase(nvidia_driver_xid_total{job="node-exporter"}[1h]))
```

liam: Shows spikes on the three nodes + a smaller bump on compute-usw-95.

devon: Hypothesis: new fw/kernel combo is exposing a marginal power/thermal corner on older A100 PCB batches. Flicker causes short recoverable ECC then a reset path for the driver -> `Xid 79`.

devon: Proposal: run a proactive burn-in and adjusted auto-drain policy for suspected hosts before we replace cards. This buys time and might avoid shipping replacement cards unnecessarily.

maya: What does the burn-in look like? Cost/impact?

devon: Plan sketch: pick 12 affected hosts across regions (6 USW + 6 EU), cordon + migrate pods, run a combined mem+compute stress for 12 hours, collect telemetry (ECC rate, temp, power, Xid). If post-burnin shows no repeat, re-enable. If repeat above threshold, schedule RMA/replace.

sanjay: Need concrete thresholds. Propose: >5 Xid events in 1h OR ECC-correctable rate > 100/min sustained for 5m -> mark as fail. Also track kernel oops count.

liam: Example burn-in commands:

```
# cordon node
kubectl cordon compute-usw-107
# drain safely (evict with grace)
kubectl drain compute-usw-107 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# run stress (containerized)
docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:11.7-base bash -lc "python -c 'import torch; a=torch.randn(1024,1024,device=0);\nimport time\nwhile True:\n a = a.mm(a); time.sleep(0.1)'" 
# memory tester
docker run --rm --gpus all ghcr.io/yourorg/cuda-memtest:latest --duration 12h
```

liam: We'll also tail `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF` and kernel dmesg.

ops-bot: Canary rollout triggered by deploy-bot: driver 525.85.12 -> rollout-window 2025-02-18T02:00Z. Notifying owners. :loudspeaker:

maya: Metrics we'll export to a temporary dashboard: ECC rate, Xid type breakdown, GPU temperature, PCI link state transitions, process name for Xid hits.

devon: Cost tradeoff — burn-in 12h on 12 hosts = 144 node-hours. If we avoid 3 unnecessary replacements (parts+swap labor) that's a win. But it delays full fleet rollback if the driver is the root cause.

sanjay: Agreed. Parallel option: quick kernel rollback on a tiny canary group (4 nodes) + simultaneous burnin on the suspected set. If rollback clears Xid on canaries, we have strong signal to revert.

maya: Can we get a smoke script to run automation? I put together a minimal checklist and script prototype:

```
# smoke-burnin.sh
NODE=$1
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh root@$NODE 'systemctl stop kubelet; docker run --rm --gpus all ghcr.io/yourorg/cuda-memtest:latest --duration 12h'
# poll metrics every 60s and push to temp GCS
```

liam: I'll wire a Prometheus alert for the thresholds so we don't miss transient spikes.

devon: Rollback criteria: if canary rollback nodes show >80% reduction in Xid rate within 30m -> schedule fleet rollback and pause further upgrades. Also require confirmation from hardware team if burnin leads to persistent bad SNR.

maya: Owner + timeline:
- devon: run the 12-host burn-in (start Thu 04:00Z)
- liam: alert + dashboard (done by Wed EOD)
- sanjay: coordinate kernel rollback canary + decide by Thu 08:00Z
- maya: liaise with hardware for RMA eligibility

devon: I'll open a ticket with the hardware vendor with logs + sample parts to pre-approve RMA if burnin fails.

maya: One more ask — please capture per-token/per-pod latency anomalies during burnin. We saw a few pod restarts that surfaced upstream timeouts.

liam: noted. We'll tag burnin runs with `burnin-202502` and include request_id for traceability.

maya: Cool. If everyone agrees I'll kick this off Thu 04:00Z. :+1:

sanjay: +1. If we see the canary rollback succeed, we pivot quickly.

ops-bot: Action created: INFRA-4127 "A100 flicker triage: burnin + canary rollback" assigned to devon, due 2025-02-21.

maya: Thanks team — followups in the ticket.
